decisionBrief.decisionNow: Choose the next discriminating study, not a presumed cause or intervention.
decisionBrief.hypothesisRule: Age is one candidate explanation. Recognition, prevention, access, follow-through, capacity, biology and measurement may coexist or interact; retain evidence against each explanation.

measurementQuestions.question: What is the population burden of late-stage disease?

decisionBrief.unknownDeltasScope: The geographic null concerns the legacy baseline; the separately versioned supplement supplies its own observed 2019–2023 contrast. Pathway and effect unknowns remain open.
decisionBrief.missingnessRule: Unknown is not zero. A valid number can answer the wrong decision question; no one measure substitutes for the others.

decisionBrief.implementationCondition: Evidence supporting a testable pathway gap or credible remediable mechanism can justify a comparative exploratory test, with uncertainty preserved and qualified oversight. Set resources, accepted ownership, eligible population, fidelity, stop rules and maintenance; do not treat permission to study as proof for routine rollout.
decisionBrief.comparison: Compare with competent current care. Select a suitable randomized or defensible quasi-experimental design; DiD or DDD requires its own identification assumptions, not only arithmetic.
decisionBrief.benefitEvidence: Appropriate resolution, patient health/function and burden, all-stage and late-stage incidence with suitable lag; harms, equity, capacity and incremental costs. Earlier diagnosis, more diagnoses or a stage shift alone cannot establish benefit because lead-time, length and stage-migration effects remain possible.
decisionBrief.signalValidation: Candidate earlier signals must precede the outcome without information leakage; qualify the instrument, validate externally for intended use and assess incremental net benefit before clinical deployment.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Some people who meet a specific cancer screening recommendation are not screened within the intended window.
hypotheses.alternative: Differences may reflect true differences in eligibility, risk, patient preference or coding rather than screening access.
hypotheses.discriminatingTest: Measure documented eligibility, offer, invitation and completion with a valid at-risk denominator, before/after plus credible comparator.
hypotheses.proposedInstrument: Site-specific EHR aggregate; guideline version; insurance; access interviews; approved registry linkage where needed.
hypotheses.ownerRole: Primary care, epidemiology, navigators and community advisers

hypotheses.hypothesis: Some abnormal screening or concerning clinical findings are not resolved promptly through the next indicated diagnostic step.
hypotheses.alternative: Documentation lags and referral leakage across systems can mimic clinical delays; urgent pathways differ by site.
hypotheses.discriminatingTest: Reconstruct result-to-contact, referral, scheduling, definitive follow-up timelines and undocumented loss to follow-up.
hypotheses.proposedInstrument: De-identified referral timestamps, procedure capacity, patient journey interviews, outcome adjudication.
hypotheses.ownerRole: Clinical pathway owner, quality lead and health information specialist

hypotheses.hypothesis: Local clinical diagnostic capacity, hours or referral availability contribute to delayed evaluation in parts of the catchment.
hypotheses.alternative: Observed wait may reflect case mix, selection, prioritization or missing external records.
hypotheses.discriminatingTest: Compare capacity, wait times and completed referrals across facilities and eligible populations, including seasonal demand.
hypotheses.proposedInstrument: Colonoscopy/imaging/pathology capacity, staff schedules, referral queues and completion data.
hypotheses.ownerRole: Health systems, specialist service lines and workforce evaluator

hypotheses.hypothesis: Transportation, affordability, paid leave, childcare, access needs or communication problems contribute to missed screening or follow-up.
hypotheses.alternative: Different risk eligibility and provider supply may explain observed geographic variation; avoid attributing differences to group identity.
hypotheses.discriminatingTest: Triangulate consented patient/CHW interviews with appointment logs and structural access measures.
hypotheses.proposedInstrument: Patient experience, language and disability accessibility, administrative barriers, travel and affordability measures.
hypotheses.ownerRole: Community co-investigators, navigators, social service partners

hypotheses.hypothesis: Some cancers present through symptoms or risk pathways for which routine screening does not apply, and delays may occur in evaluation.
hypotheses.alternative: Underlying cancer biology, interval cancer and disease aggressiveness may explain advanced stage despite timely care.
hypotheses.discriminatingTest: Audit symptom onset where documented, referral decisions, diagnostic tests and adjudicated stage by site.
hypotheses.proposedInstrument: Clinical review, tumor type, symptom pathways, diagnostic record audit and registry case definitions.
hypotheses.ownerRole: Licensed clinical reviewers and registry scientist

hypotheses.hypothesis: Apparent changes in late-stage burden may partly reflect shifts in surveillance completeness, stage coding, populations or screening intensity.
hypotheses.alternative: The change may be real, may be case mix, or an altered observation process; don't presume any one.
hypotheses.discriminatingTest: Audit registry stage definitions, source revisions, missing stage, site mix, annualized counts and age-adjustment; conduct sensitivity analysis.
hypotheses.proposedInstrument: Original registry metadata, completeness audits, Census denominators, repeat data extract, independent review.
hypotheses.ownerRole: Cancer registry methodologist, biostatistician and external reviewer

hypotheses.hypothesis: Some people may have earlier identifiable risk or clinical signals that the existing pathway misses; age is one candidate, not an established cause.
hypotheses.alternative: Biology, interval disease, prior prevention, referral loss, case mix, documentation or measurement may explain the pattern, separately or together. All-age rates cannot establish when a person should have been screened.
hypotheses.discriminatingTest: Link age, stage, prior risk information, eligibility, symptoms and care history; separately examine average-risk asymptomatic screening, higher-risk pathways and symptomatic/abnormal-result evaluation. Test interactions with access and follow-through.
hypotheses.proposedInstrument: Authorized age/risk/stage and longitudinal pathway data; pre-outcome signals without leakage; qualified instruments, external validation and incremental benefit/harm evaluation.
hypotheses.ownerRole: Registry scientist, clinical pathway lead, biostatistician and patient partners

hypotheses.hypothesis: Differences in underlying occurrence or opportunities for effective precancer prevention may contribute to late-stage population burden.
hypotheses.alternative: Detection intensity, population composition, disease biology or registration differences may change observed incidence without a local prevention effect.
hypotheses.discriminatingTest: Study age-specific all-stage incidence, prior screening and polyp detection/removal, relevant risk/context measures and stage completeness; distinguish prevention from earlier detection.
hypotheses.proposedInstrument: Time-aligned registry history, appropriate eligibility and procedure records, validated risk measures and a suitable longitudinal comparator.
hypotheses.ownerRole: Cancer epidemiologist, prevention clinician and implementation evaluator
